runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will aim to lead from flag fall; John McConnell yard in solid 3/20 recent form, 7lb claimer helps, comfortable on Good ground and over this trip but faces a direct rival for the lead in Rocky's Howya which complicates his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise when second last time out, and Jackson Lamb returns on a quick 18-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; winless in his last five starts, but that recent placed effort under 168 lb gives genuine cause for optimism.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a clear recent win and strong sim-going record (13/15); Denis Hogan's yard is 2/23 over 14 days which is respectable, and fresh off an 11-day turnaround; best served by a truly-run race where he can close off honest pace.|
runners_data.comment: Tassarolo boasts two wins in his last five starts, including a victory three starts back, and returns just 11 days later with experience of today's distance and going in his favour; the main risk is that he was unplaced two starts back and could only manage fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a win at 17f on Good and consistent sim-going figures (13/15 with 1W4P); at 9 years the jumping accuracy matters at this trip and Karl Thornton's runner arrives with a clean prep; stays well and suited to the likely race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Rich Belief arrives on the back of back-to-back thirds, retaining solid form, and he was a winner three starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 123 ranks him narrowly top of this field, though 158 lb is the chief burden he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Allo Al Khawaneej
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse but the volume of similar types means he is likely to end up racing mid-division rather than off the pace where he is most effective; sim-going figures are modest (11/14) and the trainer C Byrnes is 0/6 in the 14-day window — style compromise is the central concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Allo Al Khawaneej at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and 30 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the concern is a recent unplaced effort and a stiff 154 lb to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Bryson
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse who faces the same overcrowding issue as several rivals, placed into midfield by the pace map but unlikely to get his preferred detached position; best effort came over this trip on Good, but the 0W1P sim-going record and amateur jockey make this a difficult puzzle.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Bryson is hard to fancy, though a second three starts back and a return to familiar going at least offer slim encouragement ahead of this assignment off 154 lb.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Howya
runners_data.note: Front-runner with two wins at 24f including a recent success; Declan Queally's yard has the other runner in the race and this horse wears tongue tie and visor, suggesting it needs keeping focused; at 10 years old it retains form and is the most credentialled pace-setter in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Rocky's Howya has won twice in his last five starts and arrives on a fresh 24-day break having shown he handles today's distance and going; the concern is that unplaced efforts either side of his most recent victory suggest some inconsistency to navigate.

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: A horse whose natural style is coming from off the pace, though the field's composition means he is likely to be forced closer to the speed than preferred; Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride for T G McCourt but the trainer is 0/8 in the 14-day window and recent form reads 4090-9, limiting appeal.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pair of ninths and unplaced efforts the chief concern, Eastern Wind at least returns on a quick enough turnaround at 21 days and has experience of today's going, though 150 lb is a stiff ask for a mare yet to find her best form.

runners_data.name: Movie King
runners_data.note: OR 82 makes him the lowest-rated runner alongside Beacon Bypass; genuinely a hold-up type running out of his comfort zone in a crowded mid-division, and the trainer V C Ward has sent out no runners in the 14-day window — hard to see a winning scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Movie King faces a stiff ask here; a pair of thirds three and four starts back offers slim encouragement, but a return to unplaced last time and a hefty 150 lb to shoulder make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with the strongest sim-going record in the field (14/15, 3W4P) and experience over this type of trip; Gerard Keane's yard returned a recent winner and the visor headgear suggests the trainer is looking for a peak effort — this is the hold-up horse best placed to deliver if the race is truly run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mephisto at least returns on a quick turnaround of 13 days and has run over today's trip and going before, though a career-high 148 lb and a ranking of eighth of 14 on our figures make it hard to fancy him strongly here.

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner which carries some market interest, but recent form (F04) is patchy and the last run ended in a fall; Joshua Halford claims 7lb which helps the weight, and the horse stays this trip well (14/15 sim-going) — best suited to a truly-run race but needs rivals to tire.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Howdoyalikeherhome has experience of today's distance and going but a fall in recent form and a trainer firing at just 3% over the past fortnight are significant concerns, even if 20 days off the track suggests he returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Long Gone
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good ground and has form over the sim-going (15/15), but most recent runs are uninspiring and the horse often races closer than its hold-up tag suggests; trainer Noel C Kelly returns 1/9 in 14 days; the STYLE_FIT flag means its chance in a crowded midfield is tempered.|
runners_data.comment: Long Gone won five starts ago but has since pulled up twice and finished unplaced in her latest, making her recent profile deeply inconsistent; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 16 days between runs leaves fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Malbas
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse flagged as fading in the finish, which is a significant concern at 2m4½f; the redistribution away from the rear means he races further forward than suits, and sim-going record (15/15, 2W4P) masks the finishing concerns — Edward Buckley's yard is quiet.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of fourteen on our ratings, Malbas does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 33 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; the weight burden of 146 lb and a string of unplaced efforts are harder to look past.

runners_data.name: Oh So Charming
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 18f on Good and has a 14/15 sim-going record; but the Declan Queally yard also runs Rocky's Howya, and Oh So Charming's natural hold-up style is compromised by being forced into midfield — a 6-year-old who may still be finding her feet over this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Oh So Charming won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but ranked twelfth of fourteen on our figures, his recent record also includes an unplaced effort two starts back and a fifth three starts back, making him hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Beacon Bypass
runners_data.note: Youngest runner at 4 years old and lowest weighted at 142lbs; flagged for finishing fade and has zero wins or places from five sim-going runs — the redistribution from rear to midfield only adds to the challenge, and a 7-day turnaround after a pulled-up run is a significant caution flag.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Beacon Bypass was pulled up just seven days ago and that swift turnaround adds to the concern; he has run over today's going before, and 142 lb is no help either.

races.paceDynamic: Jackson Lamb and Rocky's Howya are the two confirmed front-runners and will fight for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop over 2m4½f on Good to Yielding ground — neither is likely to concede without a battle, so the early pace will be honest rather than suicidal but will not be slow. That sustained pressure across a stamina test of this length tends to drain the leaders before the final climb, setting up a race that typically rewards horses who can travel comfortably in behind and pick up late. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Long Gone, Allo Al Khawaneej, Eastern Wind, Movie King, Malbas, Oh So Charming, Bryson and Beacon Bypass are all genuine come-from-behind horses who will be competing for fewer positions than exist, meaning several will race further forward than ideal. The race shape favours genuine hold-up horses who have the class and jumping to close off a genuine gallop — horses like Tassarolo, Rich Belief, Mephisto and Howdoyalikeherhome are better placed to exploit the pace than the redistributed midfield types whose style fit is compromised.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Jackson Lamb and Rocky's Howya burn each other off in front and the field strings out over the final mile, leaving the principals spent before the last.
scenarios.body: The honest dual-front-runner duel ensures the race is truly run, and genuine hold-up horses who have been tracking the pace without expending energy will have the most left entering the straight; Tassarolo and Rich Belief profile as the types who thrive when the race is truly run at distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Rocky's Howya Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Howya secures a clear lead early and Jackson Lamb is unable or unwilling to match him stride for stride, allowing a manageable solo tempo.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Howya is proven at 2m4f and won over that trip, and a controlled gallop suits his profile as a horse who outstays rivals when not harried — at 10 years old he retains his jumping accuracy and is well placed with a claim-reduced weight; the moderate pace would compress the field and blunt the advantage of pure closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Squeeze Through
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners set only a moderate gallop and the redistributed midfield horses manage to find racing room in the straight despite their compromised positions.
scenarios.body: Several hold-up types forced into midfield roles may still produce late runs if the tempo is muddling, though their style-fit discount means this is a less reliable scenario; Howdoyalikeherhome, trained by Gordon Elliott with some track experience at this trip, and Long Gone are the best-credentialled of this group to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners set an overly strong gallop and one of them — most likely Rocky's Howya — finds extra reserves while rivals have over-committed chasing them.
scenarios.body: A collapse in the chasing pack would benefit the horse who has been most economical at the front, and Rocky's Howya's proven stamina at 24f is a genuine asset here; with the field crowded and hold-up horses unable to get clear runs, the front runner's stamina advantage would go unchallenged to the line.

watchPoints.text: Jackson Lamb and Rocky's Howya will contest the lead directly — watch how aggressively each jockey commits in the first half-mile, as the outcome of that duel will dictate whether the pace is honest or merely moderate.

Beacon Bypass ran only 7 days ago and was pulled up in that race; jumping safety at a 14-runner field over hurdles on Good to Yielding ground is a legitimate concern — monitor for any hesitation at the early obstacles.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Long Gone, Allo Al Khawaneej, Eastern Wind, Movie King, Malbas, Oh So Charming, Bryson, Beacon Bypass) creates genuine traffic and interference risk in the straight — watch for horses trapped wide or unable to find a gap at the third-last hurdle.

Mephisto holds the strongest sim-going record among the true hold-up horses (14/15, 3W4P) and the visor suggests the yard expects a peak run — watch whether Eoghan Finegan positions him closer than usual to avoid the anticipated congestion.

Rocky's Howya's trainer Declan Queally also runs Oh So Charming — watch for any stable booking signals in the market as the two runners represent contrasting styles and one may be preferred in the betting ahead of the off.

runners_data.name: Goin'
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has placed twice in 15 similar-going runs, best effort a third over 16f on Soft; the hind-tongue tie is noted, but the main concern is getting a clear run in a 19-runner field from the back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of nineteen, Goin' faces a stiff ask under 164 lb, though he has experience of today's going and returns on a fresh enough 26-day break.

runners_data.name: Gforcejenny
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners this 4yo Cromwell-trained mare who has been off 78 days; best effort a third on Soft and she prefers to come from off the pace, but the large, competitive field makes a clean sweep from hold-up tricky.

runners_data.name: Hatfield Hammer
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 7yo for apprentice Eoin Staples, who carries a blinkered headgear flag and has an excellent sim-going record of 15 from 15; the one course winner in the prominent group and ideally suited by a lone front-runner setting a manageable gallop.
runners_data.comment: Hatfield Hammer shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before, making him a live threat from a field of nineteen; the main concern is his tendency to disappoint, with a pulled up finish among his recent starts.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for 7lb claimer Harry Sexton — 10 days since last run is a live freshness angle — but a modest recent form string of 749604 and a lack of wins on any going makes confidence hard to justify.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Katherine at least returns on a sharp turnaround of 10 days and has experience of today's going, though a career-high 162 lb and a ranking of seventh of 19 give little encouragement she can find a way through.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three wins from 15 similar-going starts, consistently placed over 18-22f on Good; Ciaran Murphy has two wins from nine runners over 14 days and this horse's style is perfectly suited to tracking a single front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Steps In The Sand arrives in fair nick, racing just 20 days after a third two starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 161 lb against a deep field of 19 while yet to win in her last five starts are the challenges she must overcome.

runners_data.name: Memories Maker
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's 5yo is a natural hold-up horse that this field's pace distribution has pushed into a mapped midfield slot; the pony headgear flag and a modest recent P run temper enthusiasm, and racing out of role weakens its chance regardless of its natural profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up most recently, Memories Maker faces a stiff ask here carrying 160 lb, though he has run over today's going before and the 23-day break may have freshened him ahead of what looks a tough assignment ranked 12 of 19.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Stable companion to Memories Maker, also for McCann, and flagged as a horse that fades in the finish; the pony headgear flag and a form string of 0-5850 offer little encouragement, and the fade tendency is particularly damaging in a stamina race on this going.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and carrying a hefty 160 lb, Midnight Musical faces a stiff task, though she has experience of today's going and our rating of 94 suggests she holds more ability than her recent unplaced efforts fully reflect.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Serenade
runners_data.note: A genuine rear-of-field hold-up type placed twice in 12 similar-going runs including a close second over 20f on Good; displaced into midfield by the overcrowded back-markers and that forced compromise markedly tempers its realistic finishing prospect.
runners_data.comment: Whiskey Serenade arrives off a sixth last time out and is winless in her last five starts, with our figures ranking her fourteenth of nineteen runners; carrying 158 lb does her no favours, though she has run over today's trip and going before and comes here fresh enough at 20 days since her last outing.

runners_data.name: Dunany Point
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner for Conor David Maxwell; went 3rd last time over 16f on Good and has form figures of 1W5P on similar going — he will set a solo pace but his overall ability level at OR 85 means his chance of lasting home in a 19-runner field is real but limited.
runners_data.comment: Dunany Point has run over today's trip and going before, and a third two starts back shows he can mix it at this level, though he pulled up three starts back and has been winless in recent starts — 155 lb is no easy task for a runner rated 85 officially.

runners_data.name: Pillartou
runners_data.note: Paul John Gilligan's 4yo hold-up type carries a fade-in-finish warning and has never placed in three runs on similar going; pushed into a midfield mapping by the rear-group congestion, and an OR of 88 from a low base of experience makes this a risky proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a pulled-up effort among them, Pillartou is rated well below his official mark on these figures and ranks 16th of 19 in the field; experience on today's going is about the only positive to cling to.

runners_data.name: Avec Espoir
runners_data.note: Veteran 13yo prominent racer for Phillip Enright who has three career wins on similar ground; off 18 days and at OR 80 he is a model of consistency at this level but the age and recent P run suggest the well is nearly dry.
runners_data.comment: Rated 98 and ranked second of 19 rivals, Avec Espoir represents a serious threat despite being yet to win in recent starts, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour at 150 lb, though his two pulled-up efforts are the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Mr Macphisto
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from 15 similar-going runs for Ricky Doyle and Eoin Griffin; 54 days off the track with a fall in the form string, but the tongue-tie and a course-friendly style make him one to respect if jumping cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 19 on our figures, Mr Macphisto makes for a tough sell, having pulled up last time and fallen the start before; he has run over today's trip and going, and 54 days off may have helped, but 150 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Ardgillan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fade-in-finish tag, trained by M M Lynch who has no runners in the 14-day window; form string of 7900-0 and a sim-going record of only 4 from 6 are both worrying, and being forced off the back of the field compounds the challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our ratings, Ardgillan makes a tough case here, though he has run over today's going before and returns after a reasonable 18-day break carrying 149 lb.

runners_data.name: Grace's Legacy
runners_data.note: Cian Collins' 4yo hold-up mare has been off 106 days and carries a finish-fade flag; a sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 5 runs on similar ground, and the enforced midfield position from redistribution further dims her prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after a 106-day absence, Grace's Legacy carries 148 lb and is ranked well below the field on our figures, making her very hard to fancy; experience on today's going is the one slim positive.

runners_data.name: Glenriver
runners_data.note: Shane Crawley's 8yo has the highest style-fit score among redistributed horses (0.93), meaning his true hold-up style is most compromised by being pushed forward in the map; form of PPP-05 and a patchy sim-going record of 8/11 make him difficult to support regardless.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and having pulled up on three occasions in recent form, Glenriver is hard to fancy ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 20-day break carrying 144 lb.

runners_data.name: Midleton Rare
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 99, a genuine hold-up stayer who won over 24f on Good and has placed three times in 15 similar-going starts; no jockey listed is a concern, but the class and distance profile give him the strongest late-finishing claims among the closers.
runners_data.comment: Midleton Rare won four starts back but has pulled up and finished ninth and unplaced since, making his recent form a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and returns after 34 days, but 169 lb is a stiff burden for a gelding rated 99.

runners_data.name: Balinaboola Steel
runners_data.note: 14yo for A D Leahy returning after a staggering 738 days off the track with pullers headgear noted; last completed run was a 3rd at 22f on Good, but the layoff alone makes this a serious fitness question mark in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive pulls-up and 738 days off the track make Balinaboola Steel a fascinating puzzle, yet he has run over today's distance and going and our rating of 109 ranks him first of 19; a third finish five starts back hints at ability, but he needs to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Magic Hands Noel
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's 5yo has been off 223 days and all five hurdles runs have produced zeros; a fade-in-finish flag, a sim-going record of just 1 from 4 on this type of surface and the enforced midfield position combine to make a short case almost impossible to construct.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to score in recent starts, Magic Hands Noel returns after 223 days off carrying 147 lb, and with just four runs on the board she remains open to improvement as connections look to unlock her potential.

races.paceDynamic: Dunany Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and faces no meaningful pace pressure from a rival leader, meaning Kieren Buckley can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 2m4½f. The prominent types — Hatfield Hammer, Steps In The Sand, Avec Espoir and Mr Macphisto — will track behind, but none are likely to force a genuine speed duel, leaving Dunany Point to bowl along at a rhythm entirely of its own choosing. Behind them, a cluster of horses tagged REDISTRIBUTED (Memories Maker, Whiskey Serenade, Pillartou, Ardgillan, Grace's Legacy, Glenriver, Balinaboola Steel and Magic Hands Noel) are genuine hold-up types who cannot all drop to their natural rear position in a field this size — some will be forced into midfield roles against their instincts, reducing their effectiveness. The race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the lead, as a lone front-runner setting a measured pace over a stamina trip creates a perfect platform for hold-and-pounce prominent types who travel well and see out the distance, rather than deep closers who will lack the clear run or the final-furlong fuel in ground-softened conditions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dunany Point Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point is allowed to bowl along uncontested and the prominent trackers fail to reel him in at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: Buckley dictates a frugal gallop that leaves his horse fresh at the business end, and with no rival willing or able to press him early the pace never becomes punishing enough to expose his stamina limits; horses racing 2nd-4th wheel into the straight with something in reserve and the winner comes from a handy prominent position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough through the middle stages that Dunany Point weakens inside the final two hurdles and a prominent tracker swoops.
scenarios.body: Steps In The Sand and Hatfield Hammer both travel handily and carry useful sim-going records, meaning they are well-placed to pick up the pieces if the lone leader ties up; Good to Yielding over 2m4½f rewards honest galloping types who stay on steadily rather than those who need a kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Runs Through
scenarios.trigger: If traffic is kind to one of the genuine closers and a fast-finishing hold-up type threads through a weakening field in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Midleton Rare holds the strongest profile among true hold-up runners here — a winner over 24f on this going profile and OR 99 at the top of the weights — and if gaps appear late could finish with most purpose; Whiskey Serenade placed over 20f on similar ground but is racing out of its natural rear position and that compromises its realistic chance in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Late
scenarios.trigger: If the field strings out across the track, horses interfere at hurdles, and the race degenerates into a staying test that exposes weak finishers.
scenarios.body: A 19-runner handicap hurdle on Good to Yielding with a solo front-runner and an overcrowded midfield raises incident risk; survivors of a messy race could include veteran handicappers with clean jumping records and course familiarity.

watchPoints.text: Dunany Point's lead is unchallenged but his OR of 85 in a 19-runner field means any early interference or a slightly stronger pace than expected could see him capitulate at the second-last — watch how far he is clear at the top of the straight.

The 19-runner field with a congested midfield full of redistributed hold-up types creates serious traffic risk between the final three hurdles — Midleton Rare and Goin' are most at risk of getting boxed in if the field fans wide.
Balinaboola Steel returns after 738 days absent — watch the pre-race market move closely, as any drift from an expected price would confirm that connections themselves are unsure of its readiness.

Steps In The Sand and Hatfield Hammer are the two prominent types best positioned to exploit the controlled pace set by Dunany Point — if either sits 2nd or 3rd turning in, they become the primary danger to everything behind them.

Magic Hands Noel and Grace's Legacy are both 200+ days off the track with no prior winning form on this going — monitor market moves for either; a surprise gamble would be the only reason to reconsider their slim prospects.

runners_data.name: Red Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing tongue-strap, Henry De Bromhead's consistent performer runs out of his natural lead role mapped as prominent — his ability to bowl along unchallenged is the key variable; 25 days fresh and goes well on this ground with a solid sim-going record of 15/15.
runners_data.comment: Red Glory shaped well when third two starts back and is fit enough on a 25-day break, with experience on today's going lending confidence; the concern is that a fourth last time out suggests he needs things to fall right, and 166 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Chanceawetmorning
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has strong form credentials including a recent win on soft and a placed effort at this trip, making him the most dangerous prominent tracker if he can travel fluidly behind Red Glory; amateur jockey James Smith claiming 5lbs is a minor caution in a competitive heat.
runners_data.comment: Chanceawetmorning shaped well with a third last time out and has winning form in recent starts, while experience over today's trip and going adds to his claims; however, a struggling trainer strike-rate and a rating of 118 in a field of 13 temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Dreal Deal
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old hold-up specialist with a clean sim-going record and a consistent placed profile over staying trips; P J Rothwell's runner needs the pace to truly test the leaders, and at 40 days off, fitness over this extended trip merits consideration.
runners_data.comment: Dreal Deal ran a fine second two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 132 marking him out as a genuine danger; the concern is a sixth last time out that leaves him needing to bounce back, and he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Liam Swagger
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer in his prime years who wears a tongue-strap and boasts a solid recent record including two wins; William Durkan's yard has shown form recently and a good performance 28 days ago keeps him on the shortlist if he travels comfortably off Red Glory's pace.
runners_data.comment: Liam Swagger arrives on the back of two wins in his last four starts, with a second and a third since suggesting he retains strong competitive form, and he has run on today's going before; the chief concern is whether 163 lb ultimately anchors him late.

runners_data.name: Final Orders
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners this genuine hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell, but the 137-day layoff following a chasing campaign at much longer distances is a significant concern — the drop back to 2m4½f could be a positive, though the fitness question is real.
runners_data.comment: Final Orders won two starts back and rates well clear of his 12 rivals on our ratings, his experience over today's trip and going standing him in good stead; the 137-day absence is the one query, but the class is undeniable.

runners_data.name: Avalo
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh's booking for Peter Fahey lifts the profile of this hold-up type considerably; recent form includes a win over this sort of trip on good ground, though a 12th-place effort last time needs to be forgiven — going back to familiar conditions with a top jockey aboard.
runners_data.comment: Avalo showed he can win at this level, landing a victory two starts back, but has disappointed either side of it and comes into this ranked ninth of thirteen; the experience over today's trip and going is a plus, though 159 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Amateur-ridden prominent type with a consistent placed record at this level, including two seconds in recent form; F G Hand's nine-year-old has a limited sim-going sample but the pattern of finishing second suggests place claims over an outright win at this level.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but yet to win, Theflyingbee has finished second in each of her last two starts and third three starts back, arriving here fresh on 17 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; a hefty 157 lb is the main obstacle to her breaking that duck.

runners_data.name: Arctic Flame
runners_data.note: Patrick Foley's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose true running style is at the back of the field — placed in the midfield section here because the rear is congested, and that mapping mismatch (STYLE_FIT 0.93) means it may race in a compromised position; form figures 1-2 on good-ground hurdles show the ability is there.
runners_data.comment: Arctic Flame has won in recent starts and returns on a reasonable 23-day break having run over today's trip and going before, but a sixth last time out and our figures ranking her twelfth of thirteen runners make her hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Barrys Spirit
runners_data.note: Adrian Murray's five-year-old is a natural hold-up horse similarly pushed forward on the map due to field congestion; recent form includes a win over this distance on good ground, but racing out of role in a compressed race shape tempers expectations despite the youth and ability.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down on our figures in a 13-runner field, Barrys Spirit has been unplaced on his latest start and has managed just one win in his last five, making him hard to fancy at the weights with 155 lb to carry, though he does have going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Heroes Rise
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy returns to the saddle for Gordon Elliott's unexposed six-year-old who has been off the track for 514 days — the long absence is the dominant factor here, and while the form prior to that break showed consistent placed efforts, fitness over 2m4½f after such a break must be questioned despite the strong booking.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts and returning after a 514-day absence, Heroes Rise faces a stiff ask, with his trainer in particularly poor recent form; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 123 offers some encouragement for a bold show.

runners_data.name: Serienmond
runners_data.note: Amateur-ridden prominent type with a modest recent run of form figures including a sixth and a ninth; Gary McGill's six-year-old has a useful sim-going record of 14/15 but the form line does not suggest it can make an impact at the business end of a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Serienmond has run over today's trip and going before, yet he remains winless in his last five starts with finishes no better than fifth, and 154 lb is a stiff ask; the drop to 25 days since his last outing at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: Five-year-old from Eoin McCarthy's yard who is a natural prominent racer but finds himself mapped to midfield because prominent berths are oversubscribed — the style mismatch (STYLE_FIT 0.92) means he may struggle to land in his preferred position and recent form figures of F, 0 and 5 do little to encourage confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a fall also blotting his recent copybook, Elusive Ogie faces a stiff ask from 152 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 24 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh, but his profile makes him very hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: John McConnell's six-year-old carries a tongue-strap and is a genuine front-runner or prominent type who will be squeezed back from his natural position by the traffic ahead — the redistribution means he races out of role, and while the yard has been in reasonable form at 3/20 over 14 days, the form figures of P, P, 7 and 4 suggest consistency is an issue.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-ups in her last four starts make Camlin Park extremely difficult to trust, and she ranks last on our figures among today's thirteen runners; the sole bright spot is a win five starts back and some familiarity with today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Red Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival looking to press from the outset, is set to control proceedings from flag to finish at a sustainable, metronomic gallop over this 2m4½f on Good to Yielding ground at Bellewstown. Chanceawetmorning, Liam Swagger, Theflyingbee and Serienmond will track closely in the prominent berths, creating a compact early order, while the hold-up brigade of Final Orders, Avalo, Dreal Deal and Heroes Rise will need to travel through traffic to land a blow. This field contains more pace-hungry types than the race shape can accommodate — Elusive Ogie and Camlin Park are natural prominent racers who are likely to be shuffled back into midfield against their will, while Barrys Spirit and Arctic Flame, true hold-up horses, are similarly displaced on the map. The sustainable, uncontested gallop set by Red Glory narrows the gaps between sections but ultimately favours resolute, well-positioned prominent horses who can travel into the pace and pick off the leader without needing a sprint finish — horses that can sit just off the lead and produce a clean round of jumping stand to gain most here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Red Glory Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Red Glory bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but undemanding pace that blunts the closers' finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Red Glory dictates from the front on Good to Yielding ground, with Chanceawetmorning and Liam Swagger tracking just off the pace and ideally placed to challenge at the last; the inability of hold-up types to close from further back in a non-searching gallop makes this a race for the prominent brigade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is deceptively strong enough to string the field out and leave prominent horses vulnerable to a late surge.
scenarios.body: Final Orders or Avalo, both genuine hold-up types comfortable on this going, would be delivered with a well-timed run from deep to pick off the fading leaders; Dreal Deal, despite age, has the course experience and staying profile to benefit if the tempo truly drains the prominent runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Helps Tracker
scenarios.trigger: If Red Glory's lead evaporates under pressure from the jostling prominent pack in the middle section, causing a scramble.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of Elusive Ogie and Camlin Park into midfield means they may push forward anyway and inject unexpected pressure, tightening the race mid-way and handing an advantage to a horse like Chanceawetmorning who can adapt and respond quickly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuinely searching gallop that burns off all the fancied names and leaves the field vulnerable to a fresh-legged runner.
scenarios.body: Serienmond or Arctic Flame, both at bigger prices and relatively unexposed in this company, could land a surprise if fatigue levels the field; Arctic Flame's natural hold-up style, though mapped to midfield here, means it arrives late with energy if the pace has truly been fierce.

watchPoints.text: Red Glory's unchallenged lead is the race's hinge point — if anything disrupts the front-runner's rhythm early, notably Camlin Park or Elusive Ogie pushing forward against the pace map, the entire race shape changes dramatically.

Heroes Rise returning from 514 days off for Jack Kennedy and Gordon Elliott is the wildcard booking of the race — monitor the market moves closely as this horse is lightly raced and could be significantly better than its price suggests if fit.

Final Orders is 137 days absent and faces a substantial drop in trip after chasing at 30f — Keith Donoghue may ride it prominently to compensate for ring-rustiness, which would add unexpected pressure to Red Glory if it parks up close.

The congestion of hold-up types (Final Orders, Avalo, Dreal Deal, Heroes Rise, Arctic Flame, Barrys Spirit) all needing to find room in the home straight means traffic incidents and bumping are likely — horses with clean jumping records and room on the outside will be at a premium.

Mark Walsh's booking for Avalo stands out in a race dominated by amateur and conditional riders — Fahey's runner is the only one combining a top-level professional jockey with a legitimate hold-up profile, making it the most interesting late runner to track through the race.

races.name: PANDA Mares Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: A hold-up mare for Gordon Elliott and Jack Kennedy with solid Good ground form (7 from 7 on similar going, 1 win 3 places); trips here are short of her best historical distances but her stamina and late-running style suit the expected race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Ranked sixth of seven on our figures and burdened with 157 lb, Ardeen Joy faces a stiff task, and a trainer firing at just 3% in the last fortnight does little to inspire confidence, though she has winning form in recent starts and experience of today's going in her favour.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: Lightly raced but progressive five-year-old for Danny Mullins who won last time out 11 days ago; form is exclusively over shorter trips (12-13f) so this 2m1f is an unproven step up in distance on Good to Yielding, and she will naturally look to race prominently.
runners_data.comment: Daboya arrives here in good heart, a winner last time out just 11 days ago, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions — the chief concern is whether 157 lb at this level stretches her stamina under a testing burden.

runners_data.name: Easter Bonnet
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained mare with Brian Hayes aboard and a win at 17f on Good ground in her record; ran 4th last time over the same trip, and her prominent style will see her in early contention, though she must navigate the positional battle behind Speisialta.
runners_data.comment: Easter Bonnet arrives here on the back of a win 23 days ago, a trainer firing at 31% over the last fortnight, and experience over today's trip and ground — though a hefty 157 lb is the obvious test of whether she can defy the burden.

runners_data.name: Fastnet Crystal
runners_data.note: J J Slevin partners this JP O'Brien-trained hold-up mare with a good placed record (sim-going: 3/4, 1W 3P) and a win over 18f; tagged as a hood-and-tongue-tie runner, she travels from the rear and this race shape should play to her strengths if she jumps fluently.
runners_data.comment: Fastnet Crystal arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a close second last time out, boasting experience over today's trip and going; carrying 157 lb is the one question, but as the top-rated runner in this field of seven she looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Radar Ahead
runners_data.note: McCourt's mare has one win from 15 similar-going runs and is racing here with a 45-day break; although she naturally wants to race prominently, the congestion of prominent types in this field means she is unlikely to achieve that position and may find herself racing in unfamiliar mid-pack territory, tempering her chance.
runners_data.comment: Radar Ahead has run over today's trip and going and, rated 108, represents a genuine danger from a field of seven, but she remains winless in her last five starts and that persistent inconsistency is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, trained by Anthony John Black and ridden by 5lb claimer Eoin Staples; won over 18f at this track on Good ground, wears hood and tongue-tie, and should dictate an uncontested lead — her chance is entirely dependent on how sustainable she can make the early gallop.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures and carrying a hefty 157 lb, Speisialta is hard to fancy despite her win last time out; she has experience over today's trip and going, but a refusal in her recent record is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Celtic Alliance
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's lightly raced four-year-old, 125 days off the track, with a win over 16f on Soft and a third over 20f on Good; carries 3lbs less than rivals and Danny Gilligan's claim could be an asset if she handles the step back up in class fresh.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back, Celtic Alliance brings live form to this but 125 days off the track and a trainer firing at just 3% recently give real cause for pause, with 154 lb no help either.

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a 5lb claiming allowance for Eoin Staples, is expected to stride into an uncontested lead and dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m1f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Bellewstown. Daboya, Easter Bonnet, and Celtic Alliance are all genuine prominent types and will compete for the ground just behind the leader, meaning the early order will be competitive between them rather than truly pressured at the front. Radar Ahead is a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that position given the number of rivals with the same instinct, pushing them further back than ideal. This race shape — a lone, unhurried pace-setter with a cluttered midfield — strongly favours hold-up horses who can travel smoothly and produce a sustained late run from off the pace, as well as any prominent runner quick enough to track Speisialta without becoming embroiled in the positional battle behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Speisialta Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta leads uncontested at a fair clip and the prominent pack neutralise each other, giving hold-up runners a clean run to the line.
scenarios.body: Speisialta sets a metronomic pace with Daboya and Easter Bonnet scrapping for supremacy just behind, creating enough sustained gallop to suit those coming from further back in the final two flights.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya or Easter Bonnet manage to get a clean lead position early and race in Speisialta's slipstream without burning fuel.
scenarios.body: A prominent horse that avoids the early scrimmage parks smoothly behind the leader and produces a decisive move from the second-last, before the hold-up runners can organise their run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Speisialta Front-Runs And Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta bowls along at a modest clip and the talented Jamie Staples pilots a controlled jumping display that is never threatened.
scenarios.body: The prominent pack fail to close down the leader in time as the pace is too steady for hold-up runners to generate enough momentum from the rear, and Speisialta's hurdling rhythm proves decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sluggish Pace Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early tempo degenerates into a dawdle and the race collapses into a sprint finish at the last flight.
scenarios.body: With no true pace injection until the final stages, runners who handle quick transitions and have sharp jumping benefit, making class and recent fitness the decisive factors over tactical positioning.

watchPoints.text: Radar Ahead is a natural prominent racer who will struggle to get her preferred position in a field this congested with front-seeking types — monitor her for early signs of becoming unsettled or forced wider than ideal as the race develops.

Celtic Alliance returns from 125 days off the track for Gordon Elliott and has only two hurdles runs to her name; if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness at the first few hurdles, her chance will evaporate quickly in a seven-runner field with no room for error.

Daboya races over 2m1f for the first time having only run over 12-13f previously — watch whether Danny Mullins allows her to stride forward naturally or conserves energy, as a stamina question at this trip is real and could see her fade from the penultimate flight.

Speisialta's 5lb claiming jockey Eoin Staples is key to the race shape — if he sets an overly modest gallop trying to preserve the leader, the race could turn into a sprint finish that neutralises the hold-up runners entirely and disrupts the probability of Scenario A.

Easter Bonnet has a pull-up on her form card (the P in 1P-041) and pulled up at Hexham over 16f on Soft in her most recent run over Heavy ground — watch her body language in the paddock and early in the race for any sign she is not fully at ease on this occasion.

races.name: John Purfield Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Collins/Gilligan combination, 23 days fresh and handles Good ground (6 from 6 sim-going runs placing), but a 20f trip last time out hints at a horse finding his ceiling; needs a strong pace to close from the rear in a field where that gallop may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Codger's Rock shaped with promise when second three starts back, and he arrives here fit on a 23-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and a hefty 166 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Garrick Painter
runners_data.note: Fitted with tongue-tie, six-year-old who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish; one win from 15 runs on similar ground and 61 days off the track for Noel Kelly — the layoff needs to be overcome before his hold-up style can be trusted in this modest pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Garrick Painter arrives with experience of today's distance and going, and that win three starts back keeps him firmly in the picture; the concern is a 61-day absence and two below-par efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Direct Approach
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone pace-setter and structural pivot of this race; Gordon Elliott-trained four-year-old ridden by Jack Kennedy handles Good To Yielding well (6 from 7), but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a reminder that his form profile reads better in a different positional context — here he sets the terms rather than runs his best race.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last four starts, Direct Approach at least has a third two runs back to his name and has run over today's going before, but a struggling trainer at 3% and a hefty 165 lb to carry make progress hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Tuckmill
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer for Fahey who has a remarkable 3 wins and 4 places from 15 Good-ground runs; 35 days off and headgear (p) noted, and while his best form is some way back, his proximity-running style makes him structurally well-placed if Direct Approach does the donkey work.
runners_data.comment: Tuckmill has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him clear of this field, but he arrives winless in his last five starts — including two pull-ups — and connections will need to see a sharper display at the weights carrying 164 lb.

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type who won 18 days ago (1/16f/GOO) for Murphy/Finegan — that recent winning form stands out and he handles Good ground (1W2P from 8 runs); claiming jockey claims 5lb and the horse's closing style needs a genuine gallop but he arrives here in the best current form of the hold-up division.
runners_data.comment: Convincing won last time out to advertise his current form, but his record in recent starts also features two unplaced efforts, and our rating of 87 suggests he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals carrying 161 lb today, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Masego
runners_data.note: Consistent four-year-old for McConnell with 1W4P from 12 similar-ground runs — a horse who repeatedly finishes in the places rather than winning; the hold-up approach suits a horse who travels well but his finishing kick may not be enough from the rear when the leader is ungiven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked seventh of 18, Masego at least brings distance and going experience to the table, though 161 lb is a notable burden and that recent run of midfield placings suggests he'll need to find more to challenge seriously here.

runners_data.name: Let It Settle
runners_data.note: Thomas Hughes runner with zero wins from 12 Good-ground starts in the hist sample, placed once from mid-pack; the name is apt but an inability to force the issue from the rear in a slow-pace shape is a structural negative, and his form string (0-0268) shows no sign of a winning effort approaching.
runners_data.comment: Let It Settle showed promise when second three starts back, but her last two runs have been disappointing eighths and sixths, and she remains winless in recent starts; she has experience over today's trip and going, though 156 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Dictionary Corner
runners_data.note: Eoin McCarthy's five-year-old is a true hold-up horse whose actual racing style sits further back than the midfield slot shown here; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) reflects the squeeze — recent PP results and a string of 6th-and-worse finishes over 19-20f make this an awkward ask at the shorter trip.
runners_data.comment: Dictionary Corner has pulled up on each of her last two starts and is winless in her last five, with our rating of 73 ranking her 16th of 18 in this field; the one positive is she has run over today's going before, but she makes little appeal.

runners_data.name: Zarushio
runners_data.note: Tom Dreaper runner back after 105 days off — the lengthy absence is the immediate red flag; a finisher who fades (⚠) with a string of 0-0000-0 and STYLE_FIT 0.90 in a slow-pace race makes it hard to construct a winning narrative even accounting for freshness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14 of 18 on our figures, Zarushio faces a stiff task here; 105 days off the track adds a fitness query, and while he has run over today's trip, that weighty burden of 151 lb gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Chesterbaylad
runners_data.note: Won 23 days ago (1/17f/GOO) for Markham with Josh Williamson (3) aboard — recent winning form is the hook; genuine hold-up type who fades, but 14 from 15 Good-ground runs placed tells you he competes and his sim-going record gives slight credence to an each-way interest in a stronger-pace outcome.
runners_data.comment: Chesterbaylad won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but his rating of 78 ranks him eleventh of eighteen and his form before that win was inconsistent, with a fourth, seventh, and second in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Lunar Landscape
runners_data.note: Coyle's six-year-old is a true rear-ranger pushed into a midfield slot by sheer weight of hold-up horses in the field; 0W from 15 sim-ground runs (5P) and recent form of 00-604 underlines a horse that finishes without winning — the redistribution only deepens his structural problem.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lunar Landscape at least returns on a sharp 16-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going to call on, though 148 lb and a ranking of tenth of eighteen suggest he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Won 1/17f/GOO in recent form (0-P189) for Denis Hogan — the blinkers are a significant headgear flag and the win at 17f on Good ground is relevant; fader tagged, but 20 days fresh and a horse whose form has been improving through the summer, making him one of the more interesting hold-up types despite positional constraints.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive ninth and eighth-place finishes make Backinabit hard to fancy at the foot of the ratings, and his record in recent starts offers little encouragement despite a win three starts back; experience over today's trip and going is the one small plus.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Mullins in the saddle for Budds is the headline, but the form string (0P-69F) including a fall and a pulled-up is deeply uninspiring; TP headgear fitted and a STYLE_FIT 0.91 discount apply — 11 days between runs and a 0W record from 15 Good starts make the booking hard to leverage.
runners_data.comment: Crypto Crash has had a turbulent time of late, falling last time out and pulling up four starts back, leaving his recent form under a cloud; he has run over today's distance and going before, but winless in his last five starts and carrying 144 lb, the tasks ahead look considerable.

runners_data.name: Avandra
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's six-year-old runs in TP headgear and has shown 0W2P from 13 similar-ground starts; the form (820534) reads as a horse rattling around mid-division — his true hold-up style is further back than the map shows, and in a shape where closers are structurally disadvantaged he looks to need significant luck in running.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 17 of 18 on our figures, Avandra is hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable 141 lb and having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a win at 2/17f/GOO on record (0-60260) for Barcoe — 10 days between runs is very tight and a Reserve jockey booking (Harry Sexton 7lb claimer) is less than ideal in a field of 18; genuine closer who needs the pace to be real, which this shape does not guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, Surviving Murmansk is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and was second three starts back — a slender thread of encouragement for connections.

runners_data.name: Turlough Abu
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for V T O'Brien whose form reads 9-875 — never finishing better than fifth in five runs — and the O'Brien yard is 0 from 1 in the T14 window; a fader with a Reserve jockey booking and no wins on record, facing a step up in opposition for a horse who has shown no indication of breaking his duck here.
runners_data.comment: Turlough Abu is unexposed and open to improvement, yet to win in her last four starts, but lightly raced enough that better may be forthcoming; back after 20 days and carrying 145 lb as she bids to find more form.

runners_data.name: Paymelater
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Millar who is a genuine hold-up horse repositioned to midfield because the back of the field is over-subscribed; wearing a hood (p) and ridden by a reserve jockey, with 0W2P from 13 similar-ground starts (46-706) — the structural squeeze and jockey uncertainty combine to make his chances hard to assess at a meaningful price.
runners_data.comment: Paymelater arrives here in good order on a 17-day turnaround, has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 99 marks him out as a serious contender in this field — the risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Owl's Delight
runners_data.note: Prominent-style seven-year-old for Donohoe who is tagged as a fader and has zero wins or places from 6 Good-ground starts (F8P-60 form); Reserve jockey and a 10-day turnaround — while his P-style means he could at least track Direct Approach, the persistent fade flag and blank record here make him a structural also-ran.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up and a fall among them, Owl's Delight carries 149 lb off an official mark of 81, and while our rating of 88 suggests some unexploited potential, his recent jumping frailties are a clear concern.

races.paceDynamic: Direct Approach is the lone confirmed front-runner in an 18-horse field and, with no natural rival to press him, Jack Kennedy can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 2m1f trip on Good To Yielding ground at Bellewstown. The redistribution note is significant: Paymelater, Dictionary Corner, Zarushio and a cluster of other genuine hold-up types are shown in midfield purely because the field is saturated with horses who prefer to race towards the rear — they will not reproduce their best racing from that mapped position. Tuckmill (P-style) and Owl's Delight (P-style, fades) add some peripheral prominence presence but neither poses a serious front-running threat to Direct Approach's position. The resulting race shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter over a sharp two-mile-plus trip — is a classic setup that rewards prominent racers who can travel just off the leader and pounce, rather than true closers who need a strong gallop to reel horses in from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Direct Approach Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Direct Approach is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged and Kennedy sets an honest but manageable pace.
scenarios.body: Direct Approach dictates every yard, uses the Good To Yielding ground efficiently, and the field strings out behind him with hold-up horses never landing a serious blow from deep; horses who can race prominently just behind him are best placed to mount any challenge in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Direct Approach's sectionals begin to tell in the closing stages and a horse tracking him closely bursts clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: With a sustainable but not slow gallop set, a horse camping just behind the leader in second or third position needs minimal stamina reserves to accelerate past at the second-last; this shape benefits horses with a prominent style who are fresh enough to sustain a run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring closers into the race in the final two flights, collapsing the advantage of the front pair.
scenarios.body: A legitimate late-run scenario requires the gallop to be stronger than a lone front-runner would naturally set, so this shape is the least structurally supported; horses like Masego or Chesterbaylad with genuine finishing form are the primary beneficiaries if it materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Punished By Dawdle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the entire hold-up division is left with too much to do turning in on Good To Yielding ground.
scenarios.body: With the majority of this field mapped away from their natural positions and unable to get a true hold-up run, a genuinely slow tempo deepens the disadvantage for redistributed horses and the race becomes a sprint finish for those near the front.

watchPoints.text: Direct Approach's race — if Jack Kennedy is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged at a comfortable clip, the field's saturated hold-up profile means no one may be organised close enough to catch him in the straight.

Tuckmill's prominent style is his single biggest asset in this race shape and bears close watching early; if he settles just behind Direct Approach, his exceptional 3W4P record on Good ground over this trip makes him the clearest danger to the front-runner.

Convincing is the freshest winning form in the hold-up division (won 18 days ago) and if the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring closers into it, Eoghan Finegan's 5lb claim makes him a live threat from the back half of the field.

The sheer volume of redistributed horses — Paymelater, Dictionary Corner, Zarushio, Backinabit, Lunar Landscape and others — means the midfield will be heavily congested early; watch for traffic problems between the 6th and 4th flight as horses jockey for position without their natural racing room.

Backinabit's blinkers application is worth monitoring at the start — horses fitted with headgear for the first time or in recent form can jump out sharply and disrupt the anticipated race shape, potentially pushing the pace higher than Direct Approach would prefer.

races.name: John Purfield Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Mc Swagger
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Phillip Enright with a tendency to fade late; five sim-going runs have yielded zero wins and just one place, and the ⚠ fade flag compounds a pattern of running on into minor positions rather than winning.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and unseated two runs back, Mc Swagger yet to find his best, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 104 positions him third among 17 — the risk is that his recent form offers little to build on.

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes over for Gordon Elliott, always a significant upgrade in ride quality; won at 17f on Good in recent form and the sim-going record of one win and one place from ten runs over comparable trips makes this the standout profile.|
runners_data.comment: Tropical Twist won two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, returning fit on 17 days' rest and carrying 168 lb off an official mark of 100; the main concern is her trainer's current run of form at just 3% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Premier Rogue
runners_data.note: Noel Meade handler returning from 87 days off; best recent finish was a third on Soft over 16f which stamps him as a stayer who handles cut in the ground, and three placings from nine sim-going runs suggest consistent if not explosive form.|
runners_data.comment: Premier Rogue is the top-rated runner in the field and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he arrives winless in his last five starts and an 87-day absence is the obvious query against him.

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton runner who fades in the finish and whose natural style sits at the back of the field — bumped into a midfield mapping because this field has too many hold-up types to show them all correctly; the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 reflects genuine concern about racing out of role.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a sixth, two other struggles, and an unseating rider on his recent cv, Kome Dans Un Reve is hard to fancy ranked 12 of 17 on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going and returns on a fair turnaround of 13 days.

runners_data.name: Laurie Blue
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with headgear flagged, whose best effort in this form string was a fourth 47 days ago; a genuine hold-up mare squeezed into the midfield representation by sheer weight of similar-type numbers, and her 1W1P from 14 sim-going runs contains a win on Good that is worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up on her most recent outing 47 days ago, Laurie Blue carries 160 lb on a return that at least sees her back over familiar distance and going, and a rating of 109 makes her one to watch if she can recapture earlier form.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the race by recent form — 3223 is a model of placed consistency and four placings from 15 sim-going runs; the headgear notation (hp) and a 5yo profile for John McConnell with Eoin Staples in the saddle makes this a prominent racer who could track Centaq honestly.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts — third last time out, and runner-up on two occasions before that — Syosset has run over today's trip and going, though he remains winless in his last five and a hefty 160 lb is the challenge to overcome.

runners_data.name: Colin's Friend
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old returns after a mammoth 204-day absence, which is the longest layoff in the field; a horse whose natural position is off the pace but whose redistribution into midfield signals it will struggle to find that spot in a 17-runner race.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after a 204-day absence, Colin's Friend carries 159 lb on a stiff enough ask, though he has run over today's trip before and our rating of 102 suggests more ability than his official mark of 91 implies.

runners_data.name: Kashel Spring
runners_data.note: Four-year-old stepping up markedly in trip — previous five runs are all at 10-16f and now faces 17f on similar ground; the 8-day turnaround is very quick, sim-going record over longer trips is thin, and the true hold-up style mapped to midfield adds another question.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Kashel Spring has been winless in her last four starts but returns just eight days after her latest outing, and lightly raced fillies of her profile can still surprise once things click.

runners_data.name: Grennanstown Lady
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane handler with 57 days between runs; the fade flag and a pattern of double-figure finishes in five recent runs make this a horse that would need everything to go perfectly, and the redistribution out of a true hold-up berth makes that even less likely.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 11 of 17 on our figures, Grennanstown Lady faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns after 57 days with that experience at least in her favour.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: Thomas Coyle runner whose entire recent form string (0-0866) and five-run hist show no finish better than sixth; all runs are on Good and the sim-going record of zero wins and zero places is a blunt summary of current ability relative to this class.|
runners_data.comment: Frontier Rose has run over today's trip and going before, though she arrives winless in her last five starts and her recent string of mid-to-rear finishes gives little encouragement; at 151 lb, the weight is another hurdle, even if our rating of 96 suggests latent ability.

runners_data.name: Centaq
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the race — Alix Balfe (7) takes the ride for Dermot McLoughlin and gets a completely uncontested lead in a field of hold-up horses; the STYLE_FIT note for Centaq reflects that it is racing into prominence not out of it, and the 43-day break is a minor query.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of seventeen, Centaq at least has experience of today's trip and going and a run over today's conditions to draw on, though 43 days off and 148 lb on his back make this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle's five-year-old has five consecutive sim-going runs all on Good with zero wins and zero places; a natural hold-up horse relocated into midfield purely because the map ran out of space, and Sean Flanagan cannot compensate for a form profile that has never threatened.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Cinnabar Moth has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 12-day turnaround, though carrying 148 lb is a stiff ask for a mare rated 80 officially, despite a stronger rating of 94 suggesting she retains ability.

runners_data.name: Vairue
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran for Ms Helen Markham, last seen ten days ago; the form string includes a Fall and a ninth, and sim-going returns of just 1W1P from 15 comparable starts points to a horse that retains some ability but needs things to fall perfectly at an advanced age.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and yet to convince over the bigger obstacles, Vairue does bring distance and going experience to the table and a 10-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh, though 148 lb is no help and his rating of 93 leaves him mid-pack of 17.

runners_data.name: Doyen Og
runners_data.note: Adrian Sexton's seven-year-old was out just ten days ago and the form string (0-P787) shows a couple of seventh-or-better finishes; another horse whose natural position is off the pace but who cannot secure it in this field, and the fade tag adds to the concern over trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, Doyen Og faces a stiff task here, with a pulled up and finishes of seventh and eighth the recent pattern; she has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Xquise
runners_data.note: The only runner without a jockey listed in the data, which is a practical concern in itself; the form string (76/0) and a hist of finishing tenth-plus repeatedly on soft and Standard suggest this horse is some way below the level required to feature here.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Xquise is yet to win in her last three starts but remains lightly raced, and returning after 22 days off carrying 161 lb, she should strip fitter and could still have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's four-year-old with no jockey declared; four runs all over 19-23f on Good suggest a stayer, but the 970P form string and four sim-going runs all showing placed-or-worse at best means this is a horse finding its level rather than threatening the finish.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and pulled up most recently, Sonna Lady is hard to fancy ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, though she has run over today's going before and 17 days between runs suggests she returns reasonably fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Centaq is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure from any other natural lead horse — this creates a lone, uncontested gallop from the front at a sustainable tempo on Good To Yielding ground over 2m1f. With Centaq able to dictate every stride through the jumping and control the fractions, the race will be run at a measured, honest but not frenetic pace, meaning the lead and prominent positions will carry a significant premium. The field is overwhelmingly stacked with hold-up types, and the redistribution note is important: Laurie Blue, Kome Dans Un Reve, Kashel Spring, Colin's Friend, Grennanstown Lady, Cinnabar Rose, and several others are all natural hold-up horses who will find themselves shuffled further back than ideal in a 17-runner field, unable to secure the prominent positions their best form requires. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: prominent runners who can track Centaq through the race and quicken from a handy berth are heavily advantaged, while the mass of hold-up horses will face a wall of traffic and a pace that does not stretch far enough to bring them into it late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centaq Controls, Chasers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Centaq leads uncontested and sets a comfortable gallop, allowing the horses just behind to travel smoothly into contention at the last.
scenarios.body: Centaq's lone front-running role hands control entirely to its camp, and the horses best placed to win are those with the pace and the tactical position to travel in Centaq's slipstream and challenge from two out; on a track where a controlled gallop rarely suits closers from deep, the principals will come from the top three to five in the running order.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to tie up Centaq and any prominent challengers, allowing the better-quality midfield horses to close decisively from the home turn.
scenarios.body: This would require Centaq to go faster than its natural rhythm suggests, or for a couple of prominent horses to push it harder than expected, creating a genuinely run gallop that unravels the leaders before the last; horses with the class to pick up in the straight and the stamina for soft-ish ground would benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field fans wide enough on the run-in to allow true hold-up horses a clear run through to challenge.
scenarios.body: Most of the hold-up horses in this field have been redistributed in the map and are unlikely to find their natural position in a 17-runner field; this scenario is discounted accordingly, as the majority of genuine closers will be stuck in traffic without the pace scenario to bring them home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Centaq blunders or tires abruptly, causing a scramble and opening the race up for any horse that has been travelling sweetly in midfield.
scenarios.body: This is an unlikely but non-negligible scenario given the tight handicap nature of the race and the jump-heavy format; it would most benefit horses who have been travelling comfortably mid-division without expending energy chasing a pace that collapsed.

watchPoints.text: Tropical Twist — Jack Kennedy's booking for Gordon Elliott in a race dominated by hold-up horses is a sharp stable move; watch whether Kennedy positions him prominently early to exploit the lone-pace scenario created by Centaq.

Centaq — the single pace-setter in a 17-runner hurdle ridden by a 7lb claimer; any jumping error, pressure from an unexpected source, or mid-race hesitation could unravel the entire pace map and make the race chaotic.

Syosset — consistent placed form (3-2-2-3) and headgear suggest a horse trained to peak at this trip; watch how Eoin Staples places him in the early stages, as getting behind Centaq at a handy distance is the key tactical move.

Colin's Friend — 204-day layoff for De Bromhead in a 17-runner handicap is worth monitoring for market support; if heavily backed on return, it signals stable confidence despite the long break and redistribution concerns.

Traffic danger in the home straight — with 17 runners and the overwhelming majority mapped as hold-up types, interference or a logjam on the run to the last is a genuine risk that could randomly eliminate a fancied runner regardless of how the pace scenario unfolds.
